title: Editor E6 slice: a block tile is dragged in the Space page builder rail, by a mouse and by a long press on touch
detail:
Split from PROG-E6 on 2026-11-23: the first item still open after PROG-E6G, a drag (mouse and long press) in the Space page builder (components/entity-blocks/space-canvas). Same gating as the builder had: the Space settings page and its owner-checked draft save; the node store only while render_path_space_profile is on. No flag or access change; EDITOR_CANVAS and EDITOR_COLLAB are untouched.

Premise re-tested (ADR-1082) on main at ed587011: true. The rail had keys and buttons only: no tile was draggable, no element in the rail carried a landing place, and the canvas model had no operation that takes a place (a column and an index). The website Layers long press hook lived under components/sites/editor, so it was website-only.

What now works. A tile in the rail is dragged to a place inside its own column, or to a place in another column of the same section. A mouse drags it by its header (the browser's own drag, as the website Layers do); a finger or a pen holds it still for LONG_PRESS_MS and then drags, through the one long press hook, which moved to lib/builder/use-layer-touch-drag.ts and is now used by both builders (the website shell changed one import line). The thresholds are the shared ones in lib/builder/gesture.ts: a move past the slop before the press lands is a scroll, so a scroll never starts a drag. Every tile (the place just before it) and every column (its end, so an empty column can be filled) carries its target as data through lib/sites/editor/layer-touch.ts, and both pointers end in one drop. The rule is dropMoveTarget and moveNodeTo in lib/entity-blocks/node-ops.ts: the order inside a column is the shared reorder rule, a drop on the place the block already has moves nothing, another section is not a landing place, and a column at the 12 block cap refuses as the Move button does. Both canvas stores answer through it (dropTarget and dropAt on the canvas model), so a drop saves through the builder's one draft write, saveSpaceGridLayout, and nowhere else. Mid drag the dragged tile dims and a line shows where the block will land; a full column says it is full instead. Escape, or letting go off every landing place, ends the drag with nothing moved. A screen reader hears where the block went, or that it stayed where it was. The keys and the Move left and Move right buttons from PROG-E6G are unchanged.

One addition to the shared hook, so the website Layers get it too: Escape lets go of a block held by a long press (a pen, or a tablet with a keyboard).

VERIFIED: nine unit tests on the rule (lib/entity-blocks/node-ops-drop.test.ts); eleven component tests on the rail measuring the store and what the draft save is sent, on both stores (space-canvas-drag.test.tsx); the website Layers tests and the layer-touch tests pass unchanged; driven in Chromium on a throwaway harness page of the shipped editor at 390 (touch emulation, long press), 1280, 1440, 1920 and 2000, light and dark: a drop into the other column, a reorder inside a column, a swipe that moves nothing at 390, Escape mid drag with a mouse that moves nothing, no sideways scroll, no page error. Pictures (mid drag and after the drop) in /mnt/project-files/editor/e6-drag/. NOT VERIFIED: on the live Space settings route with a signed-in owner and a real database save; on a real phone (touch here is emulated); in Firefox or Safari; with a screen reader.

Known limits, stated plainly: a drag stays inside the block's own section (another section is Up and Down on the section, or remove and add); the drag is in the rail, not on the canvas frame; there is no auto scroll while a block is held near the edge of a long rail; on touch the hold starts on the tile's name, not on its Up and Down buttons.

verify.note: Runs the shipped node-ops drop operation on a Space page document, the Space write guard and the shared long press state machine, nothing replaced. Fails on main: the node store has no drop operation. Passes when a dropped block lands before the tile it was dropped on, lands in another column of its section with its words, fills an empty column, moves nothing on its own place or in another section, a full column refuses, an Events section at its cap is dragged and survives the write guard, a moving finger is a scroll and a still hold arms, and the rail wires the mouse drag and the shared long press hook to that one drop on both canvas stores.
